Oh what an evening. Earlier this week a friend offered me tickets to a live podcast interview where Sarah Natochenny (the voice of Ash Ketchum from Pokémon) would be present.

Being my (one of my several) birthday weekends and the fact that Monday will be 25 years since I got Pokémon Red Version, I happily obliged.

There was a preview of a Pokémon Parody Musical (@ballsmusical) as well as the "Who's That Pokémon?" podcast. I was together with friends from the Queens Jewish Project (where I do periodic cantorial work and singing).

The hosts of the podcast spent an hour talking about Togepi and reacting to its various lore snippets (they've been doing it with every Pokémon going down the list). At the very end they asked if anyone would like to make the argument that Togepi should replace Pikachu as a Pokémon mascot.

As someone who knows nothing of stage fright, I obliged and went on the show to make that argument and boy was the exchange one to remember. And I also won an actual Togepi toy for being such a chutzpahnik. (It was recorded and will be available before you know it.) 

Sarah didn't actually show up that evening but legendary regardless.

Is Junk food a new Balenciaga in the world of wine pairing?

Thinking about champagne you eventually picture in your mind a spoon filled up with caviar followed up by oysters from west coast. And it is a great pairing indeed but it got so boring. Champagne is a hip trendy drink and requires more these days, younger generation wants more than bougie snobby ambience. It’s like no one wants to open a restaurant in UES because it’s not cool, the same with Dior - not cool anymore.

A little bit of science here - general rule is that the food affects wine. Salt and acidity in food decrees the perception of acidity and bitterness in the wine and increase sweetness and fruitiness. And in general those two food components are best friend for most of wines.

My favorite champagne pairing is either pop corn or classic salty chips which makes wine taste incredibly delicious! And look at the market right now restaurants pair champagne with fried chicken. How smart it is!

It’s all about breaking rules and thinking out of box, not everyone can but you try! Champagne ain’t getting old and you shouldn’t.

Yesterday I ended my year by playing Olivier Messiaen’s Vingt Regards sur l’Enfant Jésus at the Frick Collection @frickcollection in New York City. It was a 150 minute experience which I will remember for the rest of my life.

Many thanks to pianist extraordinaire Mika Sasaki @mikcat_piano for being such a reliable page turner for all 177 pages.

And many, many thanks to the Frick and to Jeremy Ney @jezwaldo for entrusting me with performing this masterpiece to such an attentive and receptive audience. This work is one which demands both performer and listener to go to the extremities of experience: ecstasy, terror, bliss, oblivion… it asks us to go beyond ourselves, yet the rewards on the other side of the threshold are absolutely indescribable. 

In the middle of the demented fugue in the sixth movement, ‘Par lui tout a été fait’, my fingernail split and I began to bleed onto the keyboard. I made a note of it but with the adrenaline and everything else that was happening, I didn’t notice anything of note until four movements later, in the middle of these cascading chordal scales in movement 10, when I glanced down and saw blood spattered all over the keyboard. Eek! No matter - had to finish the movement…

Luckily there was an interval directly after no. 10 when it was all cleaned up and I could bandage up my finger. It looked much worse than it actually was. But you know, now I can really say I left a piece of me at the keyboard… Gx

What an incredible journey @eyepitydafu took us lucky few on yesterday @frickcollection as he performed Messiaen's 20-part meditation on the Christmas mystery. "Vingt Regards sur l’Enfant-Jésus" is among the most demanding works in the entire piano repertoire, and Fu delivered an extraordinary performance that yielded moments of awe, terror, joy and wonder. His total commitment to Messiaen's score took its toll: just before intermission, he started bleeding from his right hand, but refused to seek treatment until finishing the 10th meditation, Regard de l'Esprit de joie ("Contemplation of the joyful Spirit"). (The red splotches on the ivory-white keys made for a graphic tableau that wouldn't be out of place amongst the medieval depictions of suffering and death upstairs.) Not everyone stuck around for the full 2 1/2 hours, but those that did were rewarded with an experience that was ecstatic, mesmerizing, and completely transporting.  Kudos to the Frick and to Fu for bringing back this masterpiece back to NYC, in what I can only hope will become a new holiday tradition. #messiaen #georgefu #frickcollection #piano #christmas

First time visiting @frickcollection feels like stepping into another era. Located inside the former home of industrialist Henry Clay Frick, the museum opened to the public in 1935 and still keeps the charm and intimacy of a private mansion. Walking through the rooms feels calm and personal, almost like you’re visiting someone’s home rather than a traditional museum.

The collection is impressive, with works by Vermeer, Rembrandt, Goya, Turner, Velázquez, and Fragonard. One of the highlights is Fragonard’s The Progress of Love, displayed in a space that was designed just for it. Every room is carefully curated, letting the art and the architecture speak together.

It’s important to know that photos and videos of the artworks are not allowed, which actually makes you slow down and pay more attention to the details around you.

A beautiful stop in New York for anyone who enjoys art, history, and a quieter museum experience. 🖼️✨

Some of the most critical work often goes unseen. Beneath the lawns and planting beds of the new garden spaces @frickcollection is a full waterproofing and roofing system designed to protect the museum and its galleries below.

Our team @knsrestoration installed the structural substrate and waterproofing layers that support the reception hall planters, garden court perimeter, and landscaped courtyards. These areas required careful detailing, strict inspections, and precise sequencing with other trades.

The completed gardens sit above a fully protected and insulated roof system that will serve the museum for decades.

@mcwhorterfamilytrust @frickcollection Within the continuum of sacred patrimony, certain works stand not as isolated objects, but as custodians of living history.

Many of the masterworks presented in “To the Holy Sepulcher: Treasures from the Terra Sancta Museum” bear direct and profound lineage ties to the Frick Collection’s permanent holdings affirming a shared custodianship of ecclesiastical, royal, and cultural legacy.

At the center stands a resplendent Throne of Eucharistic Exposition, flanked by silver and gilt candlesticks and vessels of exceptional craftsmanship. Commissioned by King Philip IV of Spain and bestowed upon the Church of the Holy Sepulcher, the work embodies the convergence of faith, sovereignty, and artistic devotion its historical gravity echoed in Diego Velázquez’s 1644 portrait of the monarch, preserved within the Frick Collection.

Such works remind us that heritage is not merely preserved it is entrusted.

There’s something about holiday family photos that reminds you of how time moves, even when you’re too busy to notice it.

At one point in life, the house is full; kids are running around, adult laughter fills the air while the music plays in the background, there’s noise everywhere. 

Then, before you know it, as that season changes— so do the holidays. The kids grow up. They move out and start families of their own. The elders grow old or move on to the afterlife. And that once rowdy house grows quieter. Simpler.

I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately, especially as I look at my family holiday photos. 

As the eldest in my family, caregiving was part of my life early on. I helped my parents with my younger sisters. I also helped my grandparents, whom as immigrants didn’t speak English yet.

Today, life looks different. I’ve grown up. I have a small family of my own. And I’ve realized that I’ve always been a part of what’s often called the sandwich generation; before I’d look after my sisters, and now it’s caring for my own child while also supporting my aging parents and grandmother. 

Being in the sandwich generation is something not many people talk about until they’re living it. 

Regardless of the immense weight of responsibility, I am grateful for blessings within it.

I’m blessed to be in a position where I get to support my whole family. And, because of I’ve always embraced this role with pride, I’m honored to support, not just mine, but other people’s families in the best way I know how. 

I am grateful to help them honor the past while preparing for the future.

These photos may look like simple holiday memories. But to me, they represent a captured moment in time in the full circle of family life. 

Happy Holidays to you all. May you cherish these moments with your loved ones and honor the memories of the past🎄

Parents really do set the example! 💪❤️ 

A landmark study by Moore and colleagues found that children with two active parents were nearly 6× more likely to be active compared to kids of inactive parents. Later research by Zecevic confirmed similar results, showing that strong parental support made kids over 6× more likely to be highly active. 

It’s not just genetics - it’s the daily habits kids see at home. When parents move, kids learn that movement is a lifestyle, not a chore. 

The research is crystal clear: children of active mothers were 2× more likely to be active, while children of active fathers showed a 3.5× increase in activity levels. But when BOTH parents were active? The effect skyrocketed to nearly 6× more likely.
 
This isn’t about forcing kids to exercise - it’s about creating a culture where physical activity is simply what families do. Children naturally model what they observe daily at home.
 
The impact extends far beyond childhood. Physically active children are much more likely to become active adults, meaning your daily workout isn’t just improving your health - it’s potentially setting up your child for a lifetime of wellness. 

Every time you choose to exercise, go for a walk, or play actively with your kids, you’re teaching them that movement matters. You’re their first and most influential role model 🧑‍🧒‍🧒 

 
Sources: Moore et al., “Influence of parents’ physical activity levels on activity levels of young children” J Pediatr (1991) 

PMID: 1993947. Zecevic et al., “Parental Influence on Young Children’s Physical Activity” Int J Pediatr (2010) PMID: 20671967.

This was my second time visiting Farm Italy in New York,my first experience was at their Huntington location last year and I was so excited when I heard they opened a new outlet in Westbury. Since it was our wedding anniversary, choosing Farm Italy to celebrate felt like the perfect decision, and it absolutely was.

From the moment we walked in, the warm interior and soft lighting created the perfect cozy, romantic atmosphere. The decor feels thoughtfully designed, modern yet inviting, making it an ideal place for a special occasion.

The hospitality and service were just as impressive. The staff was attentive, welcoming, and made us feel truly taken care of throughout the evening.

We also ordered one of their cocktails,a passion fruit martini mixed with orange it was refreshing, well-balanced, and the perfect start to our meal.

Now the food,simply outstanding. We started with the Fritto Misto Calamari, which was perfectly crisp and flavorful. For our mains, we ordered the Pappardelle Beef Bolognese and the Branzino Filet. Both dishes were absolutely delicious, branzino definitely a 10/10. We were so full by the end that we couldn’t fit in dessert, but everything we had was exceptional.

To top it off, the restaurant surprised us with a complimentary anniversary Prosecco, which was such a thoughtful touch and made the evening even more special.

I would highly recommend Farm Italy Westbury if you’re looking for a beautiful place to celebrate a special day with your loved ones. We can’t wait to go back! 💛🍝🥂
